messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: POC trial planning: model selection & multilingual support

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC:

Summary of needs:
- Use case: customer support summarization + response suggestion for English + Spanish + Portuguese
- Volume: ~5000 chats/day; latency target < 400ms p50 for suggestion generation
- Success criteria:
  * F1/ROUGE-style accuracy vs. your labeled evaluation set >= 0.78 for English and >= 0.7 for Spanish/Portuguese
  * Avg suggestion latency <= 400ms at baseline load
  * No PII leakage in outputs (we will run red-team prompts)

Proposed POC scope (6 weeks):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + infra prep (Redwood Dedicated sandbox) — owner: Marissa
2) Weeks 1-2: Model selection & integration + test dataset ingestion — owner: Aditya
3) Weeks 3-4: Eval runs (benchmarks + multilingual checks) — owner: Aditya / Ben
4) Week 5: Tuned config + fallback policies + quality review — owner: Ben
5) Week 6: Report-out + decision meeting — owner: Marissa / Priya

Model selection (initial suggestion):
- Primary: Llama-2-13b-chat (intended for instruction-following; quantized to 4-bit for cost)
- Fallback: Falcon-40B-Instruct (higher-capacity, fallback for edge-case accuracy)

Questions for you (can reply inline):
- Is the success-criteria thresholds above reasonable?
- Any additional languages we should include?
- Can you confirm a kickoff next Tuesday (Aug 25) or suggest another date?

I've attached a one-page POC plan (POC-plan-acme-v1.pdf) and a small benchmark snapshot for reference.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC-plan-acme-v1.pdf, model-benchmarks.csv

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few quick responses inline:

> Success criteria thresholds
These look fine to start. For Spanish/Portuguese, would prefer >= 0.72 if possible — our business team is more conservative there. We can be flexible but would like to see that as a stretch target.

> Languages
English + Spanish + Portuguese are primary. We have a small set of French tickets (maybe 5% of volume) — not required for the initial POC but good to note.

> Kickoff date
Aug 25 works for our team (we can do a 60-min kickoff at 10am PT).

Also: two quick technical asks for the POC:
1) Can we evaluate multilingual model behavior on code-switching examples? We have a subset of tickets with English + Spanish mixed.
2) For fallback behavior — if primary model confidence is low, we prefer deterministic routing to fallback (Falcon) rather than a safety-response.

We'll confirm attendees for the kickoff (I'll include data/ML folks). Looking forward to the plan.

—Priya

Hi Priya — thanks for the confirmation and the notes on thresholds. A few technical notes on model selection and fallback behavior: 

1) Primary model recommendation: Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit quantized)\- Pros: good instruction-following, cost-effective when quantized, reasonable multilingual competency for Spanish/Portuguese after prompt engineering\- Cons: might miss rare dialect/code-switching patterns

2) Fallback recommendation: Falcon-40B-Instruct (unquantized or 8-bit)\- Pros: stronger open-vocabulary handling, better edge-case accuracy; good as an automatic fallback where primary confidence < threshold\- Cons: higher cost and memory footprint

3) Alternative to consider: Mistral-Instruct-22B as a compromise — better multilingual out-of-the-box than Llama-2-13b in some benchmarks, lower memory than Falcon-40B. We can run a 1-day benchmark against your dataset to compare (we budgeted this in the attached model-benchmarks.csv).

4) Confidence routing + deterministic fallback: we recommend a two-check policy:
  a) If primary's token-level average logprob below X OR the reply score < Y, route to fallback\  b) Otherwise, allow primary but attach a provenance header and confidence score in metadata for auditing

5) Multilingual/code-switching: we'll create a small augmentation of your Spanish + code-mix examples and include them in the eval suite. If results show consistent gaps, we recommend an adapter/LoRA finetune on ~2-3k examples (Aditya can scope).

Next steps from our side:
- Aditya to spin up model workers and run the 1-day benchmark (target: Aug 26)
- Ben to prepare routing policy template and fallback configs
- Marissa to own kickoff logistics and reporting cadence

Happy to discuss tradeoffs on the call next Tuesday.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
